messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: high GPU queue growth detected in us-west-2 (pool: inference-large). queue_depth=12k, p95_latency_tokens=4.2s, error_rate=6%. alert_level=page

maggie (oncall): grabbing this. seeing huge queue on the large pool, customers hitting throttles. any recent deploys? :eyes:

sam (eng-runtime): not that I know of. checking driver logs now. saw a pattern of kernel-side OOMs then GPU resets. past 30m shows repeated CUDA/Xid 63 and Xid 79. past 10 nodes had driver ejects. snippet:

```
Apr 12 03:11:07 node-17 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:00:1): 79
Apr 12 03:11:08 node-17 kernel: NVRM: GPU watchdog: scheduling timeout
Apr 12 03:11:09 node-17 systemd: docker.service: got signal SIGCHLD
Apr 12 03:11:09 node-17 kubelet: Evicting pods from node due to driver reset
```

sam (eng-runtime): the runtime is detecting those nodes as unhealthy and evicting GPUs, but the autoscaler is trying to replenish and failing at scale-up. digging into autoscaler logs.

kira (sre): autoscaler shows repeated create attempts that end with API error: QUOTA_EXCEEDED. cloud error: "Insufficient GPUs available for project/region" then after retries we hit scale limit for org (limit 25 -> requested 35). So autoscaler gives up and leaves queue backed up.

maggie (oncall): ok two issues: (1) driver instability reducing effective capacity, (2) autoscaler blocked by quota/limits. Immediate mitigation options?

sam (eng-runtime): for driver side we can try two quick things: 1) soft-restart the driver on flappy nodes (nvidia-smi --gpu-reset) when possible, 2) cordon + drain really noisy nodes and mark pool size down so scheduler stops allocating there. But manual resets are flaky if kernel bug persists.

kira (sre): for scale side we can: a) temporarily shift routing off the large pool to smaller pools/models (reduce memory per-request), b) bump the autoscaler max if org quota allows, c) open emergency quota request with cloud. c will take hours. We can do a +manual fallback routing change now.

miguel (support): tracking customer impact. two customers show 504s and elevated latencies on dedicated endpoints. i'm drafting an outbound note (non-technical) to say degraded service and mitigation steps in progress.

maggie (oncall): plan: 1) enact routing fallback: route 30% of traffic for susceptible routes to our medium pool (less mem) and enable model-derate (lower batch sizes), 2) mark the most-flapping nodes for cordon/drain, 3) open cloud quota request and contact account rep, 4) if nodes keep flapping, scale down large pool to avoid churn; 5) handoff to night oncall with checklist. I'll execute routing change now.

deploy-bot: routing-change executed: 30% -> inference-medium for routes: /v1/generate (tag: canary-derate-197654). rollout: 30% immediate, 5min ramp for remaining.

sam (eng-runtime): routing change confirmed. p50 latency dropped slightly, queue depth reduced by ~18% already. attaching a quick kernel workaround we can try on live nodes:

```
# attempt soft reset on affected GPU (careful: kills processes)
sudo pkill -f \"model-server\"
sudo nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0 || echo \"reset failed\"
# then restart model server
systemctl start model-server
```

sam (eng-runtime): running this on 3 nodes that are only serving test traffic. two succeeded, one failed with "GPU reset not supported". suspect firmware/driver mismatch.

kira (sre): autoscaler attempts log:

```
2026-04-12T03:05:22Z autoscaler: request_create_node: gpu-n1-standard-8 x10
2026-04-12T03:05:24Z cloud-api: ERROR ResourceLimitExceeded: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for project
2026-04-12T03:06:10Z autoscaler: retrying scale-up (backoff=15s)
2026-04-12T03:20:30Z autoscaler: reached max_retries -> no further attempts
```

maggie (oncall): opened cloud quota request (ticket 12345), pinged account rep on slack for expedited review. also starting manual pool resize: lowering target size of inference-large by 40% to reduce churn while we stabilize.

miguel (support): sent initial customer note to PMs for affected accounts. template: "We're seeing degraded performance in generation endpoints in us-west-2 due to GPU driver instability and temporary capacity constraints. We've mitigated some traffic and are working with infra to restore full capacity. We'll update in 1h."

sam (eng-runtime): note: there's a known driver patch on 545.x that addresses a watchdog regression. patching cycle will require node reboots. scheduling rolling patch on nodes that can be drained. risk: reboots will temporarily reduce capacity further.

maggie (oncall): decision: defer full driver patch until quota cleared or we've rebalanced. for now, do targeted soft resets + routing mitigation + manual cordon of 4 most noisy nodes. jaz, you'll take night handoff at 05:00 UTC. leaving runbook:

- current knobs:
  - rollback: revert routing canary via deploy-bot (/deploy rollback canary-derate-197654)
  - temp throttle: set per-model QPS cap (model-config -> qps=0.8x)
  - node actions: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
  - driver reset: `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i <gpu>` (best-effort)
  - contact cloud rep: ticket 12345, urgent

- oncall checklist for jaz:
  1) check queue depth and error_rate every 5m for first hour
  2) if queue not reducing, increase routing fallback to 50%
  3) if more than 10 nodes flapping in 30m, escalate to eng-runtime pager
  4) continue to update customers via support channel

jaz (next-oncall): ack. I'll take it from 05:00 UTC. please post any additional notes in the thread.

maggie (oncall): cordoned nodes node-17,node-24,node-31,node-42. drain started. queue now 7.8k and dropping. error_rate down to 3.2%.

sam (eng-runtime): observed one node where driver reset returns Xid 63 immediately after restart — marking for firmware/driver replacement. added to maintenance queue.

miguel (support): updated customers with follow-up: "We routed some traffic to alternate pools; performance is improved but still degraded for a subset of requests. Next update in 1h or sooner."

kira (sre): autoscaler backoff shows it's allowed to try again after 40m; cloud ticket pending. I've increased monitoring alert thresholds to avoid noisy pages while we stabilize (alert -> page only if queue >15k or error_rate>8%).

maggie (oncall): summary before handoff: root cause likely driver instability triggered by workload pattern -> node flaps -> autoscaler overwhelmed but couldn't replenish due to quota -> queue growth + throttle. mitigation: routing fallback, node cordon/drain, soft resets, cloud quota request, maintenance list for driver/firmware. handoff to jaz at 05:00 UTC.

incident-bot: NOTE: incident updated: status=mitigating, severity=high, runbook_link=https://internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-flap

jaz (next-oncall): taking over. I'll monitor escalation triggers and the quota ticket. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maggie (oncall): thanks all — leaving the thread open for updates and will post postmortem link when available.
